info.name: MomCare Mobile
info.description:
MomCare patient-side API for the Flutter mobile app. The hospital-staff web app (Next.js) has its own collection, `MomCare Platform`.

Setup:
1. Set `base_url` (default http://localhost:8000).
2. Sign up (Patient Signup -> Sign Up), confirm the emailed code (Verify Email), then call Auth -> Login -- it auto-saves `access_token` used by every protected request.
3. The refresh token is an HttpOnly cookie set by Login; Refresh/Logout read it automatically.
4. Fill in her profile once (My Profile -> Update My Profile). Auth -> Me says `profile_complete`.
5. Join a Hospital -> Browse Hospitals, set `organization_id` (and optionally `location_id`), then Send Request to Hospital. A request cannot be sent until the profile is complete.
6. The hospital opens her request, completes the clinical details at her visit and saves the onboarding form -- that is the approval. After that Auth -> Me returns `organization_id`, `patient_id` and (once a clinician opens a pregnancy) `pregnancy_id`; set `pregnancy_id` to use My Care Plan (her plan appears once a reading has been recorded for her; the folder is read-only -- she can see the plan, nutrition, exercise, medications, notes and earlier months, but change none of it).

7. My Readings is read-only: she sees her readings (with the 2 days / 1 week / 1 month / 3 months / 6 months / 1 year / custom filters and averages), her latest reading, the 30-day summary and her risk. Readings are entered by the hospital, never in the app.

Conventions:
- Every endpoint works WITH or WITHOUT a trailing slash.
- All endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}` except Login, Forgot/Verify/Reset Password and the three sign-up verification calls.
- IDs are UUID strings, never integers.
- A patient only ever reaches her own records; anything else resolves to 404, never 403.
- Pagination envelope on list endpoints: `{count, page, page_size, total_pages, next, previous, results}`.
- Her profile is identity only. Medical history, allergies and pregnancy dating are recorded by the hospital at her visit, never asked in the app.
- Auth and My Care Plan requests are shared with the web collection (staff use them too); keep the two in sync when they change.

request.description:
Sign in with **email + password**. No auth required.

Email is deliberately the only accepted identifier. Phone sign-in was built and then removed: a phone number has no single global format, so the same number reaches the API as `+923001234567`, `0300 1234567` or `03001234567` depending on who typed it, and an exact-match lookup authenticates only the one spelling stored at signup. Matching them properly means normalising every number to E.164, which needs a country to interpret a bare national number against — a guess the platform cannot safely make. Email has one worldwide format and no such ambiguity.

`User.phone` is still collected for staff and patients — it is contact information, not a credential.

**Responses**
- **200** — `access` token in the body, refresh token in an HttpOnly cookie.
- **400** — email or password missing.
- **401** — wrong password, unknown address, or a deactivated account. Byte-for-byte the same response in every case, so it cannot be used to discover who has an account here.
- **403** — credentials were right, but the hospital is pending/rejected/suspended (`org_status` says which); or, for a self-registered patient specifically, her email is not yet confirmed (`requires_email_verification: true` — see Patient Signup > Verify Email).

Reads the HttpOnly refresh cookie set by Login and issues a new access token. Re-reads the user's current role/hospital fresh each time, so a staff member moved to a different hospital does not keep acting as the old one until the refresh token itself expires.
Blacklists the current refresh token and clears the cookie.

The signed-in user's own identity and role.

Carries `requires_password_reset`. It is `true` for an invited staff member who has not yet chosen a password — send them to the set-password screen rather than the portal.

For a PATIENT account the response also carries `patient_id` and `pregnancy_id` (her own record and her current active pregnancy; `pregnancy_id` is null when she has none). Her app uses `pregnancy_id` to build `/pregnancies/{id}/current-care-plan/` and her readings URLs. Staff, hospital-admin and platform-admin responses do NOT include these keys, and the login response is unchanged.

**Patient accounts also get:** `patient_id` and `pregnancy_id` (null until a hospital onboards her / a pregnancy is opened) and `profile_complete` -- false means show the profile form (My Profile). Staff accounts get none of these three keys.

Change your own password while signed in -- MomCare's own addition beyond Neuro_RPM's auth surface (Neuro_RPM has no equivalent; every password change there goes through the forgot-password email link, even when signed in).

Permissions: IsAuthenticated.

Required: `current_password` (the account's real current password -- an access token proves the session was authenticated at some point, not that whoever is holding the device right now owns it), `new_password` (must differ from the current one, Django's validators).

Revokes every outstanding refresh token for this account on success -- signing in again is required afterward, on every device.

exec: // Dev convenience only: the real link only exists in the emailed body.
// If your local EMAIL_BACKEND is console/locmem, copy the uid/token pair
// out of the server log or test outbox by hand for Verify/Reset below.

request.description:
Step 1 of the password-reset flow. Names match Neuro_RPM's own auth endpoints exactly (forgot-password -> verify-reset-token -> reset-password), not an arbitrary MomCare scheme.

Permissions: AllowAny.

Required: `email`.

Always answers 200 with the same generic message whether or not the address belongs to an account -- anything else turns this into a way to discover who works at which hospital, and for a clinical system that list is worth protecting. A deactivated account gets no email at all (deactivation is how access is withdrawn; a reset link would hand it back), but the response still looks identical from the outside.

Step 1.5 (optional, additive) -- lets the frontend confirm a reset link is still good *before* showing the new-password form, instead of only finding out after it's filled in and submitted.

Permissions: AllowAny.

Required: `uid`, `token` -- both come from the emailed reset link. Purely read-only: never changes the password, never revokes sessions. Reset Password below still re-validates the token itself regardless of what this said (the link could expire in the gap between the two calls), so this is a UX layer on top, not a second source of truth.

Step 2 -- sets a new password using the emailed link.

Permissions: AllowAny.

Required: `uid`, `token` (from the emailed link), `new_password` (Django's validators). The token is Django's own reset token: signed rather than stored, derived from the user's current password hash, so it stops working the moment it's used or the password changes any other way -- single-use without a table of live tokens sitting in the database waiting to be stolen.

Revokes every outstanding refresh token for the account on success, same as Change Password.

A woman signing herself up from the mobile app. **No auth required.**

Creates an account and nothing else — **no tokens yet**. Her account has no organization and there is no Patient record; that only happens once a hospital approves a later join request.

Required: `email` (globally unique among *verified* accounts — see below), `password` (min 8, Django validators), `first_name`, `last_name`. Optional: `phone` (asked for again, and required, at the profile step).

**201 does not mean she's signed in.** A six-digit code is emailed to her; she must confirm it at **Verify Email** before she can sign in at all — `LoginView` refuses an unverified patient outright. This is deliberately the *one* signup path on this platform that gets this check: hospital owners are identity-checked by a human reviewer, and staff are invited to a specific address by an admin — neither needs an OTP on top of that.

**Retrying is safe.** If she abandons this attempt (lost the code, let it expire, mistyped something) and signs up again with the *same* email before verifying, this endpoint quietly replaces the old unverified attempt rather than saying "email taken" — an abandoned first try can never permanently lock her out of her own address. Once verified, that same email is locked for good. Address: all six fields are required -- `address_line1`, `address_line2`, `city`, `state`, `postal_code`, `country`. It is stored on her account here, once, and copied onto her own Patient record when a hospital approves her join request.

The second half of signup. **No auth required** — she has no token yet; this is what produces her first one.

Submit the six-digit code emailed to her along with `Sign Up`. On success, sets `is_email_verified=True` and returns real tokens — she's finally signed in.

**400 for every failure case** — wrong code, expired (15 minutes), already used, or exhausted (5 wrong attempts invalidates the code entirely, even to the right one afterward) — all the same generic message. Which one it was is not information worth handing to whoever is submitting codes, same reasoning as `Login`'s wrong-password-vs-unknown-email answer.

If the code expired or never arrived, use **Resend Verification Code** for a fresh one.

A fresh code, if the first one expired or never arrived. **No auth required.**

**Always answers 200 with the same generic message**, whether or not that email has a pending signup — confirming "yes, someone started signing up with this address" is itself information a stranger should not get from this endpoint. Same enumeration reasoning as `Forgot Password`.

Issuing a new code invalidates any earlier one for that account — at most one code is ever live at a time.

Her own profile -- the details she enters **once** and every join request reuses.

Permissions: IsAuthenticated + **IsPatient**. Only ever her own rows.

**When to call it:** straight after the first login (and on launch, when `GET /auth/me/` says `profile_complete` is false). If `is_complete` is false, show the profile form; `missing_fields` lists exactly which fields to highlight.

Identity only: nothing medical. Name, phone, date of birth and address are `User` columns (name and address came from sign-up); `national_id`, `blood_group` and the emergency contact are her `PatientProfile`.

**Required before she can send a join request:** `first_name`, `last_name`, `phone`, `date_of_birth`, the six address fields and all four `emergency_contact_*` fields. **Optional:** `national_id` (not every country issues one) and `blood_group`.

Response: every field above, plus `email` (read-only), `is_complete` and `missing_fields`.

Save part or all of her profile. Send only the fields being changed -- the app can save one section at a time.

Permissions: IsAuthenticated + **IsPatient**.

Returns the whole profile with the new `is_complete` / `missing_fields`.

**400** cases: a required field blanked (a given detail can be changed but not emptied), a phone number already used by another account, a date of birth in the future, an unknown `blood_group`, a malformed emergency-contact email. `national_id` may be blank. `email` cannot be changed here.

The hospitals she can ask to join. Searchable (`search`, `city`).

Permissions: IsAuthenticated. Approved, active hospitals only; only public-facing fields.

Each hospital lists its active branches under `locations` (`id`, `name`, `city`, `state`). Pass one of those ids as `location` when sending a request to be onboarded at that branch. A hospital that has not set up a branch yet returns an empty list, and then admits her to its default location.

Ask a hospital to take her on. **The body is only the hospital** (and optionally one of its branches) -- everything else comes from her profile.

Permissions: IsAuthenticated + **IsPatient**.

`organization` is required. `location` is optional: one of that hospital's active branches from Browse Hospitals; leave it out to be admitted to the hospital's default location.

The server copies her profile into the request as a frozen snapshot (`profile` in the response). Editing her profile afterwards does not change a request already sent; a request sent later carries the newer details. Nothing the client sends can alter the snapshot.

**400** with `missing_fields` if her profile is incomplete (see My Profile -> Get My Profile). **400** if `location` is not an active branch of that hospital. **404** if the hospital does not exist or is not approved (same response either way). **409** if she already has a request waiting with this hospital.

The request stays `pending` until the hospital saves her onboarding form, which may be after she visits in person. Still no Patient record until then.

Every request she has sent, with its status and the hospital's decision note.

Permissions: IsAuthenticated + IsPatient.

She has no organization, so Postgres RLS — correctly fail-closed — would show her nothing. This endpoint runs inside `bypass_rls()` with an explicit `user=request.user` filter instead: the filter, not the policy, is what keeps her to her own rows here.

Once approved, `patient_id` points at her new clinical record.

Statuses: `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, and `withdrawn` — the last meaning she was accepted elsewhere while this one was still open.

Paginated -- {count, page, page_size, total_pages, next, previous, results}, same envelope as every other list endpoint. `page`/`page_size` are optional (defaults: page 1, page_size 25, max 100).

Each row has `status` (`pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, `withdrawn`), `location` / `location_name` and the `profile` snapshot that was sent. `approved` means a hospital has onboarded her: sign in again (or refresh) and `GET /auth/me/` now returns her `organization_id`, `patient_id` and, once a clinician opens it, `pregnancy_id`.

**The patient takes back a request she has not had answered yet.** Her own token, not the hospital's.

Only works while the request is still `pending`:

- **200** — withdrawn. The slot is released, so she can apply to that same hospital again (the one-pending-request-per-hospital rule counts only pending ones).
- **404** — not her request. Scoped to her own rows *before* the lookup, so another woman's request is 'not found' rather than found-and-refused.
- **409** — already `approved`, `rejected`, or `withdrawn`. Approval created a real Patient row and a care relationship; undoing that is a discharge the hospital performs, not a POST from the phone. Withdrawing a rejection would rewrite the hospital's record of a decision it actually made.
- **403** — hospital staff calling it. Withdraw is hers alone; a hospital declining someone is a *rejection*, recorded with who decided it.

**There is deliberately no edit endpoint.** The `draft` is what staff read when deciding, so it must not change under them — otherwise they could approve details they never saw. Withdraw and send a new request instead.

Her whole current plan in one response: nutrition, exercise, the doctor's medications and notes, allergies and conditions, this week's progress, quick reading advice, the contact-your-care-team message, warning signs and a disclaimer.

Permissions: IsAuthenticated + **IsPatient**, her own pregnancy only (anyone else's is 404). The patient version never carries staff bookkeeping (who reviewed or finalized it).

`care_plan` is `null` until her first reading has produced a plan. `preparing` / progress flags in the same response say what is happening, so the app can show "your plan is being prepared" instead of an empty screen.

**Read-only.** A patient never creates or changes anything in a care plan: the plan is generated from her readings and the doctor adds medications and notes. She only reads it.

Just the nutrition section of her current plan, with its own progress summary and the sources it was based on.

Permissions: IsAuthenticated + **IsPatient**, her own pregnancy only. `care_plan` is `null` until a plan exists.

**Read-only.** A patient never creates or changes anything in a care plan: the plan is generated from her readings and the doctor adds medications and notes. She only reads it.

Just the exercise section of her current plan, with its own progress summary and the sources it was based on.

Permissions: IsAuthenticated + **IsPatient**, her own pregnancy only. `care_plan` is `null` until a plan exists.

**Read-only.** A patient never creates or changes anything in a care plan: the plan is generated from her readings and the doctor adds medications and notes. She only reads it.

The medications the doctor has added to her current plan, on their own.

Permissions: IsAuthenticated + **IsPatient**, her own pregnancy only (anyone else's is 404).

`care_plan.items` is a list of `{id, text, added_by, created_at}`, oldest first; medications the doctor has removed are not shown. An empty list means the doctor has added none. `care_plan` is `null` until a plan exists. The same items are also inside Get Current Care Plan under `medications`.

**Read-only.** A patient never creates or changes anything in a care plan: the plan is generated from her readings and the doctor adds medications and notes. She only reads it.

The notes the care team has written for her on her current plan, on their own.

Permissions: IsAuthenticated + **IsPatient**, her own pregnancy only.

`care_plan.items` is a list of `{id, text, added_by, created_at}`, oldest first; removed notes are not shown. These are the notes written for the patient to read -- staff's private monitoring notes are a different thing and are never shown here. She cannot reply to a note: if something is wrong she uses the contact-your-care-team message and her readings.

**Read-only.** A patient never creates or changes anything in a care plan: the plan is generated from her readings and the doctor adds medications and notes. She only reads it.

Every month's plan of her pregnancy, newest first -- her history, not just the current month.

Permissions: IsAuthenticated + **IsPatient**. Only her own plans. Optional `pregnancy` filter. Standard pagination envelope.

Each row is the same patient version of the plan as Get Current Care Plan (nutrition, exercise, medications, notes, ...). Use `id` with Get My Care Plan and `is_current_month` to tell the current month apart.

**Read-only.** A patient never creates or changes anything in a care plan: the plan is generated from her readings and the doctor adds medications and notes. She only reads it.

One of her own plans by id, in the patient version.

Permissions: IsAuthenticated + **IsPatient**. Another woman's plan (even at the same hospital) is **404**, never 403.

**Read-only.** A patient never creates or changes anything in a care plan: the plan is generated from her readings and the doctor adds medications and notes. She only reads it.

Her readings, newest first, in the standard pagination envelope. Each row has the vitals, `source` (device or manual) and `recorded_at`; the internal device id is not shown.

The response also carries a `statistics` block, empty unless `reading_type` is sent (see the variants below).

Filters, all optional: `period` = `2_days`, `1_week`, `1_month`, `3_months`, `6_months`, `1_year`; or `start_date` + `end_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, a custom range wins over `period`); or `since`. A bad value is a 400.

**Read-only.** Readings are recorded by the hospital (or a device), never by the patient: there is no way to add or change one from the app. Permissions: IsAuthenticated + **IsPatient**, her own pregnancy only (anyone else's, even at the same hospital, is 404). `pregnancy_id` comes from `GET /auth/me/`.

Same list, narrowed to today and yesterday. Swap the value for `1_week`, `1_month`, `3_months`, `6_months` or `1_year`.

**Read-only.** Readings are recorded by the hospital (or a device), never by the patient: there is no way to add or change one from the app. Permissions: IsAuthenticated + **IsPatient**, her own pregnancy only (anyone else's, even at the same hospital, is 404). `pregnancy_id` comes from `GET /auth/me/`.

item.name: List My Readings - Custom Date Range

request.description:
Same list, between two dates (inclusive, in the hospital's timezone).

**Read-only.** Readings are recorded by the hospital (or a device), never by the patient: there is no way to add or change one from the app. Permissions: IsAuthenticated + **IsPatient**, her own pregnancy only (anyone else's, even at the same hospital, is 404). `pregnancy_id` comes from `GET /auth/me/`.

item.name: List My Readings - Blood Pressure, Past Month (with Averages)

request.description:
`reading_type` adds the `statistics` block for exactly one group: `blood_pressure`, `temperature`, `blood_glucose`, `hemoglobin` or `wellness`.

`statistics` has `average`, `min`, `max` and `readings_count` per vital, and `categories` -- for each clinical category (for example `bp_category`) the guideline it follows and the count and percentage in each band. The same numbers the hospital sees. Blood pressure and heart rate are whole numbers; the other vitals keep one decimal.

**Read-only.** Readings are recorded by the hospital (or a device), never by the patient: there is no way to add or change one from the app. Permissions: IsAuthenticated + **IsPatient**, her own pregnancy only (anyone else's, even at the same hospital, is 404). `pregnancy_id` comes from `GET /auth/me/`.

The last reading she had. `reading` is `null` -- never an invented normal value -- if there is none yet; `total_count` is how many she has in all.

**Read-only.** Readings are recorded by the hospital (or a device), never by the patient: there is no way to add or change one from the app. Permissions: IsAuthenticated + **IsPatient**, her own pregnancy only (anyone else's, even at the same hospital, is 404). `pregnancy_id` comes from `GET /auth/me/`.

The quick card: `last_30_days_average` of every vital (`null` for a vital with no reading in the window) and `risk_this_month`, the share of her risk assessments this calendar month that were low, medium and high (`null` if there were none).

**Read-only.** Readings are recorded by the hospital (or a device), never by the patient: there is no way to add or change one from the app. Permissions: IsAuthenticated + **IsPatient**, her own pregnancy only (anyone else's, even at the same hospital, is 404). `pregnancy_id` comes from `GET /auth/me/`.

Her current risk and the last 30 days of risk history.

`current` is always the true current assessment: `final_risk_level` (`low`/`medium`/`high`) with its display text, the category of each vital (`bp_category`, `heart_rate_category`, `temperature_category`, `glucose_category`, `hemoglobin_category`), `assessed_at` and the reading behind it. `history` is the same shape, newest first, within the window (`period`, default `1_month`; same codes as the readings filters; at most 100 rows).

When the current level is high, `contact_care_team` is true and `contact_message` says to contact the care team today; every response carries a `notice` that this is an automatic check, not a diagnosis -- show it.

**Never shown to her:** the model's raw answer, its confidence, whether the assessment was flagged, its review status or who confirmed it. The staff filters (`review_status`, `flagged_for_review`, `actionable`) are ignored.

**Read-only.** Readings are recorded by the hospital (or a device), never by the patient: there is no way to add or change one from the app. Permissions: IsAuthenticated + **IsPatient**, her own pregnancy only (anyone else's, even at the same hospital, is 404). `pregnancy_id` comes from `GET /auth/me/`.

Same, with the history window widened. `period` takes `2_days`, `1_week`, `1_month`, `3_months`, `6_months` or `1_year`.

**Read-only.** Readings are recorded by the hospital (or a device), never by the patient: there is no way to add or change one from the app. Permissions: IsAuthenticated + **IsPatient**, her own pregnancy only (anyone else's, even at the same hospital, is 404). `pregnancy_id` comes from `GET /auth/me/`.
